title: Baby on the Move: Push, Pull & Ride
strapline: Push the pram, pull the wagon, ride the little car — a baby's first journeys, powered by them.
intent: Push-along toys, wagons and sit-and-ride cars give babies and toddlers safe, motivating ways to build the big movements of pulling up, cruising, walking and steering.
Pushing a walker or pram supports those crucial first steps, giving a moving handhold that builds balance and confidence.
Loading, pulling and unloading a wagon develops strength, coordination and the joy of transporting treasures from here to there.
Discovering that they can make a car or trolley move, stop and turn is early cause-and-effect and a powerful sense of agency.
Moving toys around, filling and emptying them, feeds the deep toddler urge to transport and to explore space and distance.
Journeys on the move — chasing, being chased, arriving with a delighted adult — build connection, communication and pure physical joy.
implementation: Offer sturdy push-along walkers, prams, pull-along wagons and low sit-and-ride toys on a safe, clear floor or outdoor space.
Give babies room and time to pull up, cruise and push at their own pace, staying close for the wobbles.
Add baskets, blocks and soft toys to load, push and deliver, feeding the urge to transport.
Name the movement and cause-and-effect: 'you're pushing the pram — off you go!', 'you made the car move!'
Create simple journeys and destinations — push to the mat, ride to the door — and share the arriving with delight.
Keep the space safe and open, and celebrate every new push, pull and step.
key_questions: Off you go — you're pushing the pram all by yourself!
You made the car move — where shall we go next?
Shall we load the wagon up? What will you carry?
Can you push it all the way to the mat?
Where's Grandma gone — shall we ride to find her?

impact.text: Babies gain control of their bodies in sequence — pulling up, cruising and taking those first pushing steps.
Babies push, pull and carry big things on purpose, loading and delivering treasures.
Babies explore freely with their whole body, climbing on and off and moving through space.
Babies discover they can make a car or trolley move, stop and turn — early cause and effect and a real sense of agency.
Babies use a trusted adult as a safe base to push off from and return to.

enhancements: Baskets, blocks and soft toys to load, push and deliver, feeding the urge to transport.
Simple journeys with a destination — a mat to reach, a door to arrive at — shared with delight.
A low ramp or gentle slope to feel a push roll away and change speed.
Push-along walkers and prams staged near a low rail for cruising practice.
Outdoor pushing on a safe path so the journeys get longer and bolder.

playing_exploring: Babies push, pull and ride freely, exploring movement, distance and what these toys can do.
active_learning: Babies persist at pulling up and pushing along, working hard at balance and steps, thrilled by each success.
creating_thinking: Babies begin to connect their own effort to the moving, stopping and turning, and try it again another way.
